problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Given that $A$ and $B$ are row equivalent matrices and $det(A)=-108$, find $det(B).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that $det(A)=det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $det(A)=det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form 

$$
{R}_{j}:={R}_{j}+(k){R}_{i},\,i\ne j.
$$

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$
